title: u_e (silent e)
parentNote: This is the last of the silent e vowels, and it says oo: flute, tune, June, rude. The e is quiet as always and reaches back over one consonant to change the u. The slip to listen for is the short u sneaking back in, so tube comes out tub and flute comes out flut — cover the e with your finger, read the short word, lift the finger, read it again: tub and tube, plum and plume. Say the oo with your lips pushed forward in a small circle, the same shape as yesterday's blue and glue, and tell your child that is on purpose: English has two ways to spell one sound and today they have both. One honest warning, in case they meet it in a book — cube and huge use these same letters but say yoo, not oo. That is a different job for another day, and not a mistake they made.

activities.mouthCue: Lips pushed forward in a small circle, held steady: ooo. The same shape as blue.
activities.prompt: The e on the end says nothing. It reaches back over the t and tells the u to say oo.
Two of these work on their own. One is a u with a silent e waiting at the end.

activities.text: June did make a tune on the flute, and the dog did hum.
Tim sat on a big sand dune and ate a prune!
Is it rude if a dog sits on the flute?

activities.title: June and the flute
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: June got a flute in a long blue tube.
June sat up on a sand dune and did make a tune.
The tune did drift up the hill and past the hut.
A mole came up. Then a crab. Then the dog.
The mole and the crab sat still, but the dog did not!
The dog did dig, and the dune fell in on the flute.
June did dig and dig and got the flute back.
June made a rule: the dog can hum, but the dog can not dig.
